producer_report.summary: I added `athena check --host-rules`. It reads the rulesets view of the GitHub origin, using GET requests only. It prints the existing per-rule report and then either an all-in-force line or one line per missing required rule. It exits 0 when every required rule is in force and 2 otherwise. The required rules are force-push and deletion forbidden on `athena/records`, and up-to-date required on `main`. A rule that cannot be read counts as not in force. The flag conflicts with `--history`, `--pr-head` and `--attribution`. I ran clippy for athena-cli and athena-core, and the targeted tests, `mirrors` and `policy` all pass. The full `cargo test` suite was not run, so it is left to Athena.

criteria_check.criterion: `athena check --help` / `athena --help` source in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs documents `--host-rules` in the Check doc comment and as a clap arg, so it appears in --help output.
criteria_check.evidence: Check doc comment has a --host-rules paragraph and a `host_rules: bool` clap arg; check --help output shows both.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli host_rules`: a test with fixture replies for rules in force asserts exit code 0 and the exact rendered text (athena/records: force pushes and deletion forbidden; main: up-to-date required before merge).
criteria_check.evidence: tests::host_rules_in_force_exits_0_with_the_report asserts code 0 and the full text; passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli host_rules`: a test with fixture replies where a rule is not in force asserts exit code 2 and the rendered text names the branch and the missing rule.
criteria_check.evidence: tests::host_rules_not_in_force_exits_2_naming_branch_and_rule asserts code 2 and the lines naming athena/records deletion and main up-to-date; passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core host_rules`: the fake runner records every call and the test asserts each is a GET `gh api` read (no -X, -f, --method other than GET) when invoked through the new command path.
criteria_check.evidence: host_rules::tests::host_rules_origin_path_makes_only_get_reads drives check_origin (the path the command uses) and asserts each call is exactly [api, path]; passed. The cli test also asserts two-arg calls.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing `athena check --host-rules`; display.rs holds any new rendering helper used by main.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: Entry added under Unreleased/Added; display::host_rules_report added and used by host_rules_command in main.rs.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass (tested default).
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks (I ran clippy for the two crates, fmt, the targeted tests, mirrors and policy; all pass).

open_issues: Unknown (unreadable) required rules count as failures and give exit 2.
The full cargo test suite was not run; it is left to Athena.
learnings: GhClient::origin_repository parses the owner/name of a github.com https origin URL; host_rules reuses it.
The Check dispatch opens the repository first, so --host-rules needs a git repository with an origin remote.
